title: AuMaNET — Brand & experience guide

messages: One scrollable history. The composer and navigation stay outside it.
Preserve drafts across navigation and rotation. A failed save keeps the draft and shows Retry.
Use sender names, time and device-storage status. Never imply a human read receipt.
Keep a reader’s scroll position; follow new content only when already at the latest message.
voice: Join muted. Enabling the microphone is a separate choice.
A fresh press starts hold-to-talk; release, backgrounding or interruption ends it.
Mute, received sound and Leave are distinct controls.
Show the persistent voice strip on other destinations. Applying voice settings mutes input.
map: The map fills the available screen, with controls overlaid on its edges.
Private acquisition and published location are separate actions.
Label last-known positions, age and accuracy. Do not turn stale fixes into current ones.
Inspect people or coordinates in a sheet; return to the same map view.
people: Use compact rows for people and nodes; show connected/away status in text.
Full identities and membership actions belong in details.
Invitations, approval and removal require explicit actions.
Do not infer a checked node association from a display name.
tools: Group destinations by Network, Devices and Tools.
A row is a destination; a switch changes one explicit setting.
Show the current value or status as trailing metadata, not a paragraph.
Use a back action for secondary screens. Put deeper explanations in disclosures.
maintenance: Keep preparation separate from activation or installation.
Give progress, cancellation and unknown outcomes distinct states.
An unknown result requires recheck; do not offer a blind repeat.
Show the exact relevant identity and conditions at the decision point.
forms: Persistent label above the value; 16px form text and visible focus.
Keep related fields in a short group. Hide advanced assumptions in a disclosure.
Do not erase input on background refresh or recoverable failure.
Place the primary action after its inputs; return focus after closing a sheet.

components: Title left; connection and contextual actions right. Back only on secondary screens.
Icon + text, with a sage active container. Keep active state visible.
Full row opens a destination. A 1px divider separates entries.
Incoming left, self right. 16px corners and one 4px tail corner.
Attach, multiline input and Send. Keep save feedback below the input.
Forest fill, white label. Use for the next deliberate action.
Labelled dialog, close action, inert background, focus containment and return.
Keep saved, queued, failed, unknown and read meanings distinct.
Persistent label and inline error; preserve values on failure.
Secondary explanation or advanced settings. Avoid hiding essential decisions.
stateRows: Name the missing item and give one useful next action.
Retain saved history, drafts and maps; disable only unavailable actions.
Describe the current operation and provide Cancel when possible.
Show active service state beyond its owning screen.
Keep input intact; provide an inline recovery action.
Hold the original intent. Inspect status before repeating.
Keep historical context visible without claiming freshness.
Explain the needed capability at the attempted action; support retry.
Name the consequence and the exact scope before confirming.
handoff: The approved screenshot library, rules and tokens are the visual authority. The neutral functional brief remains the capability contract.
Do not feed original-app screenshots, styles or existing navigation into further design decisions. Record any new decisions in an addendum.
Inventory actions and state contracts first. Implement them within these layouts without importing old visual structure.
App bar, five destinations, one scroll owner, keyboard-aware composer, sheets and safe areas precede decorative refinement.
Check failure, offline, stale data, unknown outcomes, cancellation and recovery as well as the happy path.
Use the same route, state and viewport. Compare geometry and interaction, then test actual devices, text scaling and assistive technology.
